messages:
jon: Quick sync — thinking through autoscaler safety + predictive warmup for Dedicated GPU pools.

maria: Can you add a one-liner about the failure mode we're trying to avoid?

jon: Mostly the spike case where we scale up predictively but run out of budget, or reactive scale being too slow and incurring SLA violations. Also tenants that have bursty but infrequent traffic.

ashok: Agree. My rough idea: keep the reactive scaler as primary, add a lightweight predictor that suggests prewarm tokens per tenant using a decaying EWMA of request rate and a periodic windowed forecast. Predictor only authorizes prewarm credits, not GPU provisioning.

kevin: How do we gate cost? Predictors sound like a money sink if wrong.

ashok: Proposal: two levers — 1) per-tenant prewarm credit cap (configurable) and 2) global safety budget (monthly). Predictor must pass both to schedule prewarm. If exceeded, fallback to reactive path.

sophie: Also need quick fallback to lower-cost model variants when capacity constrained. We should wire priority policies: SLA > best-effort > background. Lower-cost variant = quantized/short-context model.

maria: +1. We should surface the prewarm decisions in Console (why we prewarmed, credit consumed). Ops wants traceability.

jon: Example config sketch:

``
autoscale:
  predictor:
    enabled: true
    tenant_window: 10m
    ewma_alpha: 0.2
    max_prewarm_tokens: 1000
  safety:
    global_budget: 50000
    tenant_cap_pct: 0.02
```

ashok: We also need admission control when prewarming hits timeouts. If prewarm doesn't reduce tail latency within X sec, revoke and mark predictor as degraded for that tenant.

kevin: What about multi-tenant pool fairness? If many tenants prewarm, could drown smaller ones.

sophie: Use weighted headroom buckets. Allocate ephemeral headroom proportional to committed capacity + a min floor. That way small tenants always get some minimal prewarm.

jon: Ops question: how do we test in staging?

ops-bot: Deploy plan: canary predictor to 10% of traffic; enable metrics: predicted_tokens, actual_prewarm_hits, prewarm_failures, cost_impact. Rollback via feature flag.

maria: For rollout, let's run a 2-week canary with cost guardrails and a kill-switch. I'll draft the rollout doc.

ashok: Action items: (1) implement predictor feature flag + metrics, (2) add tenant cap enforcement, (3) Console visibility, (4) write e2e load test simulating bursty tenants.

kevin: I'll own (2) and (4). maria take rollout doc. jon + ashok will pair on predictor impl.

sophie: tiny nit: include a model-fallback matrix in the RFC so customers can map latency vs cost tradeoffs.

jon: Great. Linking RFC notes: https://rdrw-internal/rfcs/dedicated-autoscale-predictor (draft) :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all. We'll sync in sync-up tomorrow 10am.

kevin: thanks :slightly_smiling_face:
